messages:
Alice: Quick heads-up — I ran a profiling pass on the decode path and found recurring batch stalls when function-calls return structured outputs with trailing stop tokens. Repro on dev cluster (p3-small pool). Latency tail jumps ~3-4x for affected batches.
Ben: Can you attach the trace/flame? Is it the KV cache eviction or the scheduler blocking on I/O? :thinking:
Alice: Pasted a small extracted trace below (timestamps are relative ms):
```
0-12ms: batch formation / kernel select
12-40ms: decode tokens (continuous batch)
40-240ms: tool-call pause (waiting for tool response + stop-token handling)
240-260ms: resume decode, KV cache reattach
```
Carla: Hmm if tool-call pauses inside a batch, the runtime currently holds the whole batch's GPU stream open until resume, right? That will block other queued requests — explains tail.
Mike: Right. We batch at token granularity; a single request hitting a tool-call becomes an interrupt. Two interactions to consider: 1) queue policy (do we form batches that avoid mixing likely-tool callers with pure-decoding requests?), 2) token budget targets (smaller per-batch token caps so pauses don't bloat).
Alice: Exactly. Also saw kernel fallback when sequence length morphs after a tool-call because we pad/resume weirdly — affects kernel selection and increases per-token time by ~8%. Trace shows a kernel switch at resume (fast->compat) which is bad.
Ben: Propose experiment: try a queue policy that separates "tool-likely" requests (requests with tool_hint header) into a separate queue with a small delay window, and set max_tokens_per_batch=256 for that queue. For pure decode queue keep 1024.
Carla: Agreed. Also add a pre-check to detect stop-token heavy outputs — if the prompt contains structured-output template, prefer pessimistic KV warmup so resume doesn't recompile kernels. Could be a simple flag at request time.
Alice: Here's an example config for the scheduler experiment to try on staging:
```json
{
  "queues": [
    {"name": "decode", "delay_ms": 4, "token_budget": 1024, "policy": "pack"},
    {"name": "tool", "delay_ms": 12, "token_budget": 256, "policy": "isolate"}
  ],
  "kernel_selection": {"sticky_on_pause": true, "recompile_threshold_ms": 50}
}
```
Ben: Nice. For metrics let's capture per-batch: batch_size, pause_count, pause_duration_ms, kernel_switches, kv_attach_time. If pause_count>0 we should emit an annotated sample for eval.
Mike: One more wrinkle — stop tokens can be multi-byte sequences that the tokenizer yields mid-token, leading to extra decode token emitted and then truncated which confuses batching length predictions. We should capture predicted_remaining_tokens vs actual_received_tokens in traces.
Carla: Good call. Also consider a fallback policy: if tool-call pause > 150ms, transparently spill the remaining requests in the batch to the next batch (preemptive continue) rather than holding GPU. That requires being able to checkpoint KV state cheaply.
Alice: I can make a small patch to the scheduler (isolate queue + preemptive spill) and run A/B on staging tomorrow. Will attach perf diffs and a small script to tag requests with tool_hint for existing clients. /cc @Anita-bot to spin the deploy job when ready.
Anita-bot: deploy triggered for staging:run-1798523345-sched-expt (ETA ~15m) :rocket:
deploy-bot: perf collector attached for job run-1798523345-sched-expt. Sending samples to /mnt/perf/staging/1798523345.tar.gz
Mike: Great. If the kernel sticky flag helps we might avoid recompile thrash completely. If not, we can try sticky + quantized-compat kernel as a fallback.
Alice: Thanks all — will post results in this thread after the run. :eyes:
